clue.text: Old London show venue lures actor to perform

indicators.note: to perform suggests the letters are set to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A former London exhibition hall tempts a thespian onto its stage.
explanation.walkthrough: EARLS COURT was a large exhibition centre in west London, home to shows like the Ideal Home Show, demolished in the 2010s.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls Court Exhibition Centre hosted major trade shows and concerts for decades before closing.

clue.text: Has meal with bridge player, seconds coming later

indicators.note: coming later means the seconds letter moves further back in the word

parts.note: the four bridge players are named North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: Someone dines with a bridge partner, and second helpings follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to consume food, which is what having a meal involves.

clue.text: Cultivating fruit over middle of pergola

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the fruit sits above the next piece

parts.note: a raisin is a dried grape, a fruit

indicators.note: middle of means the central letter of the word pergola

explanation.surface: A gardener grows fruit across the centre of a pergola.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising crops or animals means growing or rearing them, which is cultivating.

clue.text: Affectionate words of love between dessert courses

indicators.note: between puts the love word in the middle of the desserts word

parts.note: sweets are dessert courses in British usage
love is nothing, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Lovers whisper tender words between puddings at a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' looks romantic but is the tennis score of nil, so it gives NOTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet nothings are the tender, trivial endearments lovers murmur to each other.

clue.text: Musical work regularly got reaction, Duran Duran hit

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, here the even ones

parts.note: Rio was a 1982 hit single by the band Duran Duran

explanation.surface: A Duran Duran hit got a reaction from listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of 'got reaction' gives ORATO.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale sacred composition for orchestra, choir and soloists.

clue.text: Go over again right speed for turning

indicators.note: for turning means the speed word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: pace means speed

explanation.surface: A driving instructor revisits the correct speed for cornering.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or restate the main points of something already said.

clue.text: Banker about to become a star

indicators.note: about means the river's name is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: a river has banks, so a 'banker' is a river: here the Avon

explanation.surface: A banker is on the verge of achieving celebrity status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' looks like someone in finance, but in crosswords it is a river, because rivers have banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares to great brightness before fading.

clue.text: Past prison sentence undermines individual

indicators.note: undermines in a down clue means the sentence goes under the individual

parts.note: an individual is one
doing time is serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A spell in jail ruins a person's life.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means former, as in a one-time champion who was champion in the past.

clue.text: Shocked at one's dish being chopped up

indicators.note: chopped up means cut into pieces, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A diner is horrified that their meal is being diced.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonished means greatly surprised or amazed, a strong shock.

clue.text: Maybe the port in Yorkshire that produces yarn?

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t', as in 'on t' moor', which is why the clue adds 'in Yorkshire'
port is an example of a wine, which is why the clue says 'Maybe'

explanation.surface: A tourist wonders whether a Yorkshire port is where yarn is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like a harbour town, but it is the fortified wine; a Yorkshireman would say 'the wine' as 't'wine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine is strong string or thread twisted from strands, a kind of yarn.

clue.text: Creator of Rich Tea crackers backed by court

indicators.note: backed by means the following piece comes behind, at the end
crackers means mad, so the letters of the biscuit's name go haywire

explanation.surface: Someone invented Rich Tea biscuits and was supported by a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: Rich Tea is a plain British biscuit; 'crackers' pretends to be more biscuits, but it means crazy and shuffles RICHTEA into ARCHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect designs buildings, and figuratively anyone who originates a plan is its architect.

clue.text: Irrelevance of trendy suit Tory is wearing

indicators.note: is wearing means the outer pieces wrap around the Tory like clothing

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a suit of cards is a set, and a sequence is a run of them
CON is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is dressed in a fashionable suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsequence is the quality of being unimportant or not following logically.

clue.text: During muster recalled soldiers needing time for self-analysis

indicators.note: During puts the other pieces within the muster word

parts.note: a muster is a formal inspection of troops

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the soldiers' letters are read backwards

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: At a parade, soldiers summoned back need time for some soul-searching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muster' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a muster is a parade where troops are checked over. 'Recalled' turns the soldiers backwards rather than summoning them.
explanation.definitionFit: Introspection is examining one's own thoughts and feelings, looking inward at oneself.

clue.text: Swimmers able to do the crawl?

definitions.text: Swimmers able to do the crawl?

parts.words: Swimmers able to do the crawl?
parts.note: the crawl suggests a swimming stroke, but the creatures meant can literally crawl on land as well as swim

explanation.walkthrough: The crawl sounds like front crawl, a stroke; here it is crawling on land, which frogs and newts can do.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphibians such as frogs and newts live both in water and on land, swimming and crawling.

clue.text: In retirement intend to purchase tall adult tree

indicators.note: retirement is going backwards, withdrawing, so the whole is read in reverse
purchase here means grip, so the aim word holds the other pieces

parts.note: to intend is to aim
tall means long
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A pensioner plans to buy a tall, mature tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying, but it also means a firm grip, which is why it signals one piece holding others; 'retirement' is a withdrawal, or moving backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a flowering tree or shrub known for its large showy blossoms.

clue.text: French city narks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a city in the Loire valley of western France
second meaning: annoys, irritates (to nark is British slang for to vex)

explanation.walkthrough: 'Narks' looks like a noun for informers, but here it is a verb meaning irritates.
explanation.definitionFit: Angers is the historic capital of Anjou; separately, the verb means makes someone cross.

clue.text: One given contract perhaps when almost impertinent throughout

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: sassy means impertinent, cheeky
in can mean throughout, as in 'in the year'

explanation.surface: Someone is hired whenever cheekiness runs nearly all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' is a business deal on the surface, but a hit-man is given a contract to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a killer hired for a contract killing of a public figure or target.

clue.text: Close to lunch, number reaching hill top?

indicators.note: close to means the end of the next word, its final letter

parts.note: eight is a number

explanation.surface: Near midday, a group of walkers reaches a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a height can be a hilltop or high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A height is a high place or elevated point, such as a summit of a hill.

clue.text: Extremely inconvenienced, unknown students I caught getting romantic

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, here Y
L is a learner, so two students give LL
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Badly put out, students of mystery identity were caught by me getting amorous.
explanation.definitionFit: Idyllic describes a picturesque, peaceful scene, romantic in the sense of idealised.

clue.text: Collect brass emblems to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone gathers a few brass badges.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather or bring together, as people or things are collected.

clue.text: Robbery from Scottish bank family reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the letters sound like the answer

parts.note: a brae is a Scottish hillside or bank; kin means family

explanation.surface: News of a theft from a Scottish bank owned by a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial but is a slope: brae is the Scots word for a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: A break-in is the forced entry of a building to steal, a burglary.

clue.text: Crazy heartless rules man obeyed excessively

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters are thrown into a new order
heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A man followed mad rules to an extreme degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle L out of RULES, leaving RUES, which joins MAN OBEYED to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond measure is an idiom for to an immeasurable, excessive extent.

clue.text: Old lady pinching occasionally not only money

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so ma grips the other letters

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, MA

indicators.note: occasionally means picking every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A mother steals now and then, and not just cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' suggests stealing, but it signals one piece holding another; alternate letters of 'not only' give OOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Moola is a slang word for cash or wealth.

clue.text: Originally rejected Liverpool comedian's chances

indicators.note: originally rejected means the first letter is thrown away

parts.note: Ken Dodd was a famous Liverpool comedian, so his is Dodd's

explanation.surface: A Liverpool comic's prospects were turned down at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd, a much-loved comedian from Liverpool, was known for his tickling stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the likelihood or probability that something will happen.

clue.text: References elements of magic act being changed initially

indicators.note: changed initially means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a conjuror's act is made up of illusions

explanation.surface: A list of references describes parts of a conjuror's show being altered.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening I of ILLUSIONS is changed to A; the clue does not name the new letter, so the definition must supply it.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusions are indirect mentions or passing references to something.

clue.text: Raw wound son ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the son's letter is left out

parts.note: wound, as in twisted along, means snaked

explanation.surface: A raw injury has been neglected by a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury, but it is the past tense of wind: a road that wound snaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw can mean bare or exposed, without covering, as naked does.

clue.text: Fire rifle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dismiss from a job

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like guns, but fire means dismiss and rifle means ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given the sack is to be dismissed; an army that sacks a town plunders it.

clue.text: Sport Neil wants to play around noon

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go about the noon letter
to play suggests the letters are allowed to move freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Neil wants a game at about midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn tennis is the formal name for tennis, a racket game originally played on grass.
